review.summary: Read-only review of the supplied excerpts: metric-registration-visit.tsx, live-metric-registration-page.ts, the live-playback-source route, and the form, LP, LP-step and viewer entry call sites. In this scope I found no new BLOCKER or MAJOR issues. The signed frame is never used for viewer authorization. Same-origin, rate-limit and viewer-credential checks still run before any binding is used. A missing or invalid frame under the controlled profile makes these surfaces fail: the pages throw and the playback API returns 503. The server builds the expected kind, method and target from the route it is handling, not from the signed payload. I'm reporting three MINOR issues. First, the server and gateway may format the expected target string differently, so valid requests could be wrongly rejected. Second, binding errors are relabelled as persistence errors. Third, when profile mode is on, the frame header is checked on some routes but not others. Not certified: the omitted credential and secret lines, the bodies of metricIngressFromRequest, metricIngressConfigured, issueMetricVisitPage and resolveTrackedLivePlaybackSource, the DB triggers and migrations, gateway behaviour, the full set of requests and entry points, and deployment. The earlier MAJOR finding on public quota and form failures is still open and is not repeated here. An empty or MINOR-only result does not certify that tests pass or that this is ready to release.

findings.area: form page L128; LP root L56/L61/L65; LP step L51/L57; viewer L131; playback route binding line
findings.issue: The server builds the expected frame target in inconsistent ways. The form page and LP root use the slug stored in the DB. The LP step and viewer pages use the incoming decoded route params, re-encoded with encodeURIComponent. The playback API uses the raw url.pathname+url.search. None of these share a canonicaliser with the gateway's signed target.
findings.evidence: `/form/${encodeURIComponent(form.slug)}` and `/lp/${encodeURIComponent(page.slug)}` use DB values. The step page uses `/lp/${encodeURIComponent(slug)}/${encodeURIComponent(stepPath)}` built from params. The API uses `url.pathname+url.search` as received. Requests whose bytes differ only in harmless ways will produce different strings: hex case in percent-escapes, characters like ~ ! ' ( ) * that encodeURIComponent leaves alone but a client may escape, Unicode normalisation, or a case/alias slug lookup.
findings.impact: Mismatches fail closed, so I see no way to forge or reuse a frame. However, under the controlled profile a legitimate visit can be rejected, and the whole registration or viewer page then errors. Synthetic M1/M2 runs could also show false gaps between frames and source rows, which skews the evidence.
findings.recommended_fix: Define one shared function that canonicalises the target, used by both the gateway and the server. Use it to choose the policy for each route: canonical DB slug or incoming path, and for the API either raw query or sorted canonical query. Apply it on every entry route, including both LP root and step, so they follow the same rule.
findings.required_test: Loopback tests with signed frames on the disposable DB for each route, covering: escaped vs unescaped reserved characters, upper vs lower hex escapes, Unicode slugs in NFC vs NFD, and slug case/alias variants. Assert that accepted and rejected outcomes are deterministic and match what the gateway manifest expects, and that a frame signed for one route's target is rejected on every other route.

findings.issue: Every error that is not a MetricVisitorError is turned into MetricVisitorError('PERSISTENCE_UNAVAILABLE'). If a binding failure thrown further down (frame replay, scope or target mismatch, missing frame for a run-owned source, or a DB trigger rejecting the frame) is not itself a MetricVisitorError, it will be reported as a persistence outage.
findings.evidence: `if(error instanceof MetricVisitorError)throw error; throw new MetricVisitorError('PERSISTENCE_UNAVAILABLE');`. The wrapper imports MetricIngressBindingError separately, which suggests it is a different class.
findings.impact: The page still fails closed, but logs and metrics can no longer tell forged, replayed or misbound frames apart from DB outages. Any retry handling keyed on PERSISTENCE_UNAVAILABLE would also treat integrity failures as transient. This weakens audit evidence for the controlled profile.
findings.recommended_fix: Re-throw MetricIngressBindingError (and any frame-integrity errors raised by the DB) unchanged, or map them to their own non-retryable code, before the generic persistence mapping.
findings.required_test: Unit test: issueMetricVisitPage throws MetricIngressBindingError, and the test asserts that issueMetricRegistrationPage propagates that class or code. Loopback DB test: a replayed frame on a registration surface is reported as a binding failure, not PERSISTENCE_UNAVAILABLE.

findings.area: wrapper early return before the configured/entry check; viewer metricEnabled gate L129-131
findings.issue: With profile mode on, the frame header is only checked on paths that will issue a visit. The registration wrapper returns early when the scope is unresolved or the keyring is missing. The viewer page skips the check when the keyring is missing or the runtime is unavailable. The playback API, by contrast, calls metricIngressFromRequest every time. So the rule that a missing or invalid header must fail when the profile is on depends on the route and its state.
findings.evidence: `if(!resolved||!process.env.LIVE_METRIC_VISITOR_KEYRING)return compose(child,null);` runs before `metricIngressConfigured()`. The viewer uses `metricEnabled && metricIngressConfigured() ? metricIngressFromRequest(...) : undefined`. The playback route calls `metricIngressFromRequest(request.headers, ...)` with no gate.
findings.impact: Admission frames committed by the gateway for these requests are never consumed or rejected, so there is no server-side signal. Also, if the keyring is missing from the process environment under the controlled profile, every registration and viewer visit silently goes untracked instead of failing. This can make a synthetic run look complete while sources are missing. It has no effect on authorization.
findings.recommended_fix: Decide on and document one rule. Either validate the frame whenever the profile is on, even when tracking is skipped, or record an explicit 'untracked by design' reason. At minimum, fail at startup or on first request when profile mode is on and LIVE_METRIC_VISITOR_KEYRING is missing.
findings.required_test: Loopback tests with profile mode on: (a) keyring unset, which should give a startup/request failure or an explicit untracked marker; (b) unresolved scope on the form and LP pages with a missing or invalid header; (c) viewer page with the runtime unavailable and a missing or invalid header. Assert the chosen behaviour, and assert that no source rows are written in any case.
